subject: Order form indemnity – SOW carveouts and evidence owner mapping
messages:
From: Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbus.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@nimbus.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form draft — indemnity carveouts and SOW boundary questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the order form draft. Our legal team had two fast follow-ups before we move this to DocuSign: 1) can Redwood confirm whether indemnity for IP infringement is intended to cover third-party claims arising from customer-provided data and custom SOW deliverables? We typically expect customer-originating data to be carved out. 2) If Redwood retains defense control for third-party claims, who on your side will be the technical liaison for evidence collection (logs, model snapshots, prompt sets)?

We're trying to lock both the scope (what gets carved out by SOW/data) and the evidence-handling process so our procurement can close by EOW. If helpful, I can share an internal evidence checklist.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — our target signature date is next Friday (6/20).

Best,
Sarah Barnes
Senior Counsel — Commercial
Nimbus Analytics

P.S. contracts@nimbus.ai included for procurement coordination.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Barnes <sarah.barnes@nimbus.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — indemnity carveouts and SOW boundary questions

Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: Redwood expects customer-provided data and customer-supplied SOW materials to be excluded from our IP infringement indemnity; we are willing to mirror carveouts in the order form to make that explicit. On defense control: Redwood proposes to retain overall defense control for third-party claims but will provide a named technical evidence liaison and make operational evidence handoff materials available.

Kimberly — looping you and Irene for proposed contract language and to decide the evidence-owner mapping. I think the cleanest approach is: 1) add an explicit SOW/data carveout clause into the order form AND 2) an appendix that maps evidence owners by artifact type (logs, model checkpoints, fine-tune datasets, prompts). That appendix can be non-contractual operational guidance but referenced in the order form for SLA/response timelines.

Sarah — can you confirm if Nimbus needs the evidence appendix to be contractually binding (i.e., part of the order form) or if a referenced operational annex is sufficient?

Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sarah.barnes@nimbus.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — indemnity carveouts and SOW boundary questions

Thanks — I attached a redline (Nimbus_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx) with two edits: 1) explicit SOW/data carveout under Section 7(b) that defines "Customer Materials" and excludes them from Redwood IP indemnity, and 2) an operational Annex A (referenced, non-binding except for response SLAs) that describes evidence ownership and the handoff timeline.

Key tradeoffs in the redline: if we keep defense control (Redwood leads) we should commit to a 72-hour initial evidence intake window and name a liaison (I volunteer our infra lead to be the contact). If Nimbus insists on making the evidence appendix contractually binding, we should narrow the liabilities and potentially add a cooperation clause limiting Redwood's obligations to reasonable collection requests (to avoid open-ended forensic burdens).

Attachment: Nimbus_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (track changes)
Attachment: Evidence_Owner_Matrix.xlsx (mapping draft)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments:
- Nimbus_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: sarah.barnes@nimbus.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — indemnity carveouts and SOW boundary questions

Sarah/Karthik/Kim — quick operational confirmation from infra/ops side. Per the Evidence_Owner_Matrix.xlsx (attached), proposed owners are:
- Requesting artifacts and logs: Nimbus (customer) by default; Redwood will collect server-side logs only when requested and with a signed forensic access form.
- Model checkpoints/fine-tune artifacts: Redwood (we host checkpoints) — we will provision read-only snapshots to Nimbus within the 72-hour intake window when ordered by legal.
- Prompt sets and customer-supplied training data: Nimbus — we will not include customer-supplied datasets in indemnity scope and will not retain copies beyond the agreed retention period.

I volunteer to be the Redwood technical liaison for collections; contact: irene_choi@redwood.com / +1 415-555-0126. If Nimbus wants the annex elevated into binding contract language, we should confirm which items must be contractual (e.g., retention windows, evidence access SLA) and which can remain operational.

Next steps: Sarah — please confirm whether an operational annex is acceptable or if you require the appendix language to be incorporated into the order form. If you want contract language, Kim and I can prepare an alternate redline that narrows tasks and liability buckets.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Security and Ops Integrations
Redwood Inference
